title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, continuing from p.96. X is a connected K-scheme with geometric point x0, and Π (also written Π0) is the profinite geometric fundamental group π1(X, x0). X'→X is a finite étale cover that is K-connected but not necessarily geometrically connected. Its geometric fibre E0 = X'_{x0} is a finite set. Γ·Π0 (really a semidirect/extension structure) acts on E0 transitively, but Π0 alone need not act transitively.

The classifying map (50)-(51). Sending x' to its stabiliser Π_{x'} gives a Π-equivariant map (50) E0 → {open subgroups of Π}, with Π acting on subgroups by conjugation. Passing to quotients gives (51): π0(E0) := E0/Π → Σ = Ssgr(Π)/Π, the set of conjugacy classes of open subgroups. These are the isomorphism types of the transitive Π-sets, i.e. of the geometric connected components of X'.

The lifting problem. An outer automorphism Θ of Π acts on Σ by transport of structure. The question is when Θ lifts to a Θ-semilinear bijection Θ̃0 : E0 → E0, i.e. Θ̃0(g·x) = Θ(g)·Θ̃0(x) for a chosen representative of Θ (cf. (46)).
- Necessary condition: the image of (51) must be Θ-stable.
- Grothendieck then sharpens this to the correct statement (52): there must exist a bijection π0(Θ̃0) : π0(E0) → π0(E0) compatible, via (51), with the action of Θ on Σ. This is a multiplicity-sensitive condition.
- Conversely, any such bijection on components lifts to some Θ̃. On each orbit, choose x_i and y_i with Θ(Π_{x_i}) = Π_{y_i} and set Θ̃(g x_i) = Θ(g) y_i. The lift Θ̃ is completely determined by its values Θ̃(x_i) on one point x_i in each component of E0. The freedom is the choice of y_i modulo the normaliser.

This is the elementary dictionary between finite Π-sets and covers, made Θ-semilinear. It serves the program of characterising which outer automorphisms of π̂1 come from Γ = Gal(Q̄/Q). The idea is to require compatibility of Θ with the whole tower of covers, including the non-geometrically-connected ones, which carry their own fundamental groupoids.

Second paragraph. Among the necessary conditions for an outer automorphism Θ of the profinite fundamental groupoid π̂1(X, I), with I ⊂ X(·) a set of base points, to come from Γ, Grothendieck says he forgot 'the most important of all'. It was so constantly present to his mind that it ended up seeming to go without saying. The next page identifies it as compatibility with the 'structures à bout', i.e. the structure at infinity / cusps: inertia at punctures, tangential (pointed local) sections. This is the modern condition that Θ preserves the inertia conjugacy classes, acting on them through a cyclotomic-type character. The margin note reads 'write the two conditions'.
errors: The first-stated condition (image of (51) stable under Θ) is not sufficient when (51) is non-injective, since multiplicities of components with the same stabiliser class matter. Grothendieck immediately corrects this to the existence of a Θ-compatible bijection of π0(E0), which is the right condition.

Θ is only an outer automorphism, so Θ̃0 depends on a choice of representative automorphism. This is harmless, since changing the representative changes Θ̃0 by the action of an element of Π, but it is left implicit.
Σ should be the conjugacy classes of OPEN (finite-index) subgroups of the profinite group. This is implicit in the notes.
Notation slips between Π and Π0 (the same group π1(X, x0)).

ideas.what: Classification of finite étale covers (possibly non-geometrically-connected) via stabiliser conjugacy classes, and lifting of an outer automorphism Θ to a Θ-semilinear automorphism of the fibre functor value E0.
ideas.modern_name: Galois correspondence for finite Π-sets / semilinear automorphisms of fibre functors

ideas.what: Necessary conditions for an outer automorphism of π̂1(X, I) (fundamental groupoid with several base points) to come from Gal(Q̄/Q), via compatibility with all covers and their components.
ideas.modern_name: Galois-type / GT-type outer automorphisms; anabelian characterisation of the image of G_Q in Out(π̂1)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse), Drinfeld, Ihara, Nakamura, Schneps et al.
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), Lettre à Faltings (1983), in programmatic form

ideas.what: The 'most important' forgotten condition: compatibility with the structure at the ends (inertia at cusps / tangential base points), announced here and treated on the next page.
ideas.modern_name: Inertia (cusp) preservation with cyclotomic action; tangential base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara, Deligne (tangential base points, 1989), Nakamura; Grothendieck in Esquisse
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (structures at infinity, Teichmüller tower)

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains an elementary lifting lemma for Θ-semilinear automorphisms of finite Π-sets, which is standard Galois-category bookkeeping. It also has a remark that the key cusp/inertia condition was forgotten, a condition well known in the later GT/anabelian literature. There is historical colour (Grothendieck admitting he omitted the most important condition because it seemed self-evident), but no new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: Last lines likely read roughly: '...j'ai oublié cependant la plus importante de toutes, avec laquelle je m'imprègne[?] ... tellement présente constamment à l'esprit, qu'elle finit par sembler aller de soi !' The machine transcription's ending '...construire ... pensant qu'elles ne suffisent pas sans doute. Mais aussi !' is wrong; the image shows '...finit par sembler aller de soi!'.
The 'I ⊂ X_{(·)}' is likely the set of base points I in the point set of X, so π̂1(X, I) is the fundamental groupoid with base points in I.
The word above 'Parmi les conditions nécessaires' is an insertion qualifying the conditions ('importantes' or similar); it is uncertain.
The margin note likely reads 'Citer/Écrire les deux conditions'.
Line 4: 'puis-supposée' is doubtful. It is probably 'l'action Θ̃ présupposée, restreinte à E0'.
